questions.question: Which statement best describes a local array in ObjectScript?

options.text: It must be declared with a fixed size before use.
It is always one-dimensional and numeric-only.
It is multidimensional, sparse, and does not need prior declaration.
It is stored on disk automatically like a global.

questions.explanation: T1.2 — ObjectScript local arrays are multidimensional and sparse, so subscripts do not need to be contiguous and the array does not need to be declared first.

questions.question: What does the following code print?

options.text: Apple
Banana
a

questions.explanation: T1.2 — $ORDER(arr("")) returns the first subscript key, not the stored value. Here the first key is "a".

questions.question: What does the following code print?
questions.code:
SET arr("a") = "Apple"
SET arr("b") = "Banana"
SET arr("c") = "Cherry"
SET key = $ORDER(arr(""), -1)
WRITE key, !

options.text: a
b
c
Cherry

questions.explanation: T1.2 — using $ORDER with the second argument -1 starts reverse traversal. $ORDER(arr(""), -1) returns the last key, which is "c".

questions.question: Given the code below, what does $DATA(arr(1)) return?
questions.explanation: T1.2 — $DATA = 11 means the node has both its own data value and children beneath it.

questions.question: After this code runs, which nodes are removed?
questions.code:
SET arr(1) = "a"
SET arr(1, "sub") = "b"
SET arr(2) = "c"
KILL arr(1)

options.text: Only arr(1) is removed; arr(1,"sub") remains.
arr(1) and all descendants under arr(1) are removed.
The entire array arr is removed.
Only arr(1,"sub") is removed.

questions.explanation: T4.1 — KILL on a node removes that node and its full subtree. arr(2) remains, but arr(1) and arr(1,"sub") are deleted.

questions.question: To pass a local array into a method for traversal or modification, which pattern is correct?

options.text: Declare the parameter as As %Array and call normally.
Use ByRef in the method signature and call with a leading . before the variable.
Convert the array to JSON first, then pass it as %String.
Use only globals because methods cannot accept arrays.

questions.explanation: T4.1 — ObjectScript passes multidimensional arrays by reference. The method must declare ByRef and the caller must use .myArray.

questions.question: What does the following code print?
questions.code:
SET arr(1) = "first"
SET arr(100) = "hundredth"
SET count = 0
SET key = ""
FOR {
    SET key = $ORDER(arr(key))
    QUIT:key=""
    SET count = count + 1
}
WRITE count, !
questions.explanation: T1.2 — arrays are sparse, so only existing top-level nodes are counted. The loop sees keys 1 and 100, so count becomes 2.

questions.question: Which statement is true when comparing a local array and a global?

options.text: A local array persists after the process ends, but a global does not.
A global uses the ^ prefix and persists beyond the current process.
Only globals can be traversed with $ORDER.
Only local arrays can use $DATA and MERGE.

questions.explanation: T1.2 — globals are persistent structures prefixed with ^, while local arrays live only in the current process memory.

questions.question: Which statements about local arrays are correct? (select all that apply)

options.text: Subscripts can be strings as well as numbers.
Sparse keys are allowed; subscripts do not have to be contiguous.
You must define arr(1) before defining arr(100).
A local array can be multidimensional.

questions.explanation: T1.2 — ObjectScript arrays support string and numeric subscripts, allow sparse storage, and can have multiple dimensions. There is no requirement to define every intermediate key.

questions.question: Which lines are valid array-copying or array-passing patterns in ObjectScript? (select all that apply)

options.text: MERGE dest = source
MERGE dest("copy") = source(1)
DO ..ProcessData(.myArray)
SET dest = source

questions.explanation: T4.1 — MERGE copies arrays or subtrees, and ByRef with a leading dot passes an array into a method. SET dest = source copies only a scalar node value, not a multidimensional array tree.

questions.question: Given the code below, which statements are correct? (select all that apply)

options.text: $DATA(arr(1)) returns 11.
$DATA(arr(1,"sub")) returns 1.
$DATA(arr(99)) returns 0.
$DATA(arr(1)) returns 10 because arr(1) has a child node.

questions.explanation: T1.2 — the parent node has both data and a child so it returns 11, the child leaf returns 1, and a missing node returns 0. Returning 10 would mean children exist but the node itself has no value.

questions.question: Which snippets correctly traverse all top-level nodes of a local array? (select all that apply)

options.text: SET key = ""  FOR { SET key = $ORDER(arr(key)) QUIT:key=""  WRITE arr(key), ! }
SET key = ""  WHILE 1 { SET key = $ORDER(arr(key)) QUIT:key=""  WRITE arr(key), ! }
FOR i = 1:1:$LENGTH(arr) { WRITE arr(i), ! }
SET key = $ORDER(arr(""), -1)  FOR { QUIT:key=""  WRITE arr(key), !  SET key = $ORDER(arr(key), -1) }

questions.explanation: T4.1 — standard traversal uses $ORDER in a loop, either forward or reverse. $LENGTH(arr) does not count array nodes, so option C is not a valid traversal pattern.
